findings.description: The Python egress check searches the original val, including heredoc bodies that were excluded from text because they are only being written as data.
findings.failure_mode: A command writing a Python file with a python3 shebang, an urllib import and a github.com URL is marked network_egress without executing that file or making any request. Because this check precedes the PR-content exemption, legitimate sessions become contaminated and are excluded from grading.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the Python check to the filtered command text and require the Python interpreter invocation to consume the matching program.

findings.cross_file_justification: The changed cell cost_usd includes only valid sessions, while evals/harness/spend.sh still sums cost_usd and ignores the new all_spend_usd field.
findings.description: The cycle spend reader does not account for the new distinction between credited session costs and actual spending.
findings.failure_mode: A cell that spends money on invalid sessions reports those dollars only in all_spend_usd. spend.sh counts zero for a cell with no valid sessions, and also omits prior attempts, overstating available headroom and allowing the cycle cap to be exceeded.
findings.suggested_fix: Update spend.sh to use all_spend_usd when present, falling back to cost_usd for older rows, before deduplicating run IDs.

findings.description: An empty took-effect.json passes the jq command successfully with no output, so the empty temporary file replaces took.json.
findings.failure_mode: The later slurpfile produces an empty array and took_effect becomes null instead of {"took_effect_record":false}. A truncated record therefore appears absent, bypassing the documented failure signal used by validity filters.
findings.suggested_fix: Require exactly one JSON object and a nonempty successful result; treat empty input as took_effect_record:false.

findings.description: The class 9 python clause `return bool(EGRESS_PY.search(val) and EGRESS_PYLIB.search(val) and EGRESS_HOST.search(val))` runs on the raw `val`, not on `text` (the heredoc-stripped form) and not per logical line. The function's own header states 'Heredoc bodies are read only when the command feeds one to an interpreter (written prose stays data, KF-046)', and check_value applies class 9 FIRST with the class 7 PR-content exemption disabled. So a non-interpreter heredoc such as `cat > review.md <<'EOF' ... the python client uses requests to call github.com without a timeout ... EOF`, or a multi-line Bash input where `python3 …`, a `grep requests …` and a line naming github.com are three separate commands, is marked contaminated {pattern: network_egress} with no exemption path. `\bpython[0-9.]*\b` matches the word 'python' in prose, `\b(?:urllib|requests)\b` matches the English word 'requests'.
findings.failure_mode: Review-catch runs whose agent writes or echoes prose about Python HTTP code against GitHub are invalidated as network-egress contamination; in a matched cell a session flagged this way is dropped (or makes --union exit 2), silently shrinking k and biasing the arm comparison.
findings.suggested_fix: Evaluate the python clause on `text` (heredoc-stripped unless an interpreter heredoc exists) and per logical line, consistent with the two clauses above it: `if EGRESS_PY.search(line) and EGRESS_PYLIB.search(line) and EGRESS_HOST.search(line): return True`. If a program inside an interpreter heredoc must be seen, scan only the bodies that count_interpreter_heredocs identifies, not the whole raw value.

findings.cross_file_justification: ablation-row.sh (in diff) redefines a 1.5 cell row's cost_usd as the sum over VALID sessions only and introduces all_spend_usd ('every dollar of every attempt'); spend.sh (also in diff) still reads only cost_usd (`c = float(r.get("cost_usd") or 0)`), so the two touched files disagree on what spend is.
findings.description: spend.sh exists to report cycle spend against the hard cap (DEC-0363). With row writer 1.5, a matched cell row's cost_usd excludes every invalid session's final attempt and every re-run attempt (ablation-row.sh: `cost_valid += num(s.get("cost_usd")) if valid else 0`, `all_spend += sum(acs)`), and an ordinary row's prior attempts live only in all_spend_usd (cost_usd + --prior-spend). spend.sh never reads all_spend_usd and dedups by run_id taking max, so none of that money is counted.
findings.failure_mode: Cycle spend is systematically under-reported once cells with an invalid session or any re-run exist (a k=3 cell with one invalid session hides roughly a third of its cost); headroom against the cap is overstated and the cap can be overrun while spend.sh reports green.
findings.suggested_fix: In spend.sh prefer the full figure when present: `c = float(r.get("all_spend_usd") if isinstance(r.get("all_spend_usd"), (int, float)) else (r.get("cost_usd") or 0))`, and document that 1.5 rows count all attempts. Alternatively have spend.sh report both runs_usd and all_spend_usd and compare the latter against the cap.

findings.description: EGRESS_TOOL `(?:^|[\s;&|(`=/])(?:curl|wget)\b` and EGRESS_GIT match the words curl/wget/fetch anywhere on a logical line, not in command position, and the line is split only on '\n', not on ';' '&&' '|'. A reviewer's search such as `grep -rn curl scripts/ | grep github.com`, `rg curl .; rg github.com .`, or `cat tools/curl-wrapper.sh # calls api.github.com` is classified as network egress although nothing leaves the sandbox.
findings.failure_mode: Benign code-search commands typical of a reviewer investigating hard-coded URLs contaminate the run under class 9, which has no exemption.
findings.suggested_fix: Require the tool token to start a simple command: split the line on `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|` and `(` and anchor curl/wget/git at the start of each segment (after optional env assignments), or reuse the existing interpreter-basename logic used for history_probes.

findings.cross_file_justification: recall-vs-defects.sh and ablation-grade.sh (both in diff) widen the citation extension to 12 characters so .loa.config.yaml.example:127 and Dockerfile.ablation:19 count; annotation-packets.sh's CITE_RX (shown in full context) keeps `\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,6}` for the review_driven label that labels_meta later reports per defect.
findings.description: The review_driven (D-7.6) detector cannot match a feedback citation of a file with a 7–12 character extension (`[\w.+-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,6}` backtracks to the previous dot and then fails on the following '.'), so hunks in exactly the files this change was made for are labelled review_driven=false even when the record branch cites them by line.
findings.failure_mode: labels_meta.review_driven is wrong for hunks in .yaml.example / Dockerfile.* style files, skewing the FR-2 label-provenance analysis in the direction the 12-character change was meant to fix.
findings.suggested_fix: Change CITE_RX (and the matching backtick-exclusion regex two lines below it in scan_text) to `{1,12}` so the three citation parsers agree.

findings.description: label_set() recognises manifests/v1/<pr>.json as the 'v1' label set, but key_set_root() (and recall-vs-defects.sh's new set_root block) only re-roots c131 keys. For a v1 key corpus_sha256 looks for manifests/SHA256SUMS (null), grade_recall reads manifests/v1/v1/<pr>.json for the v1 snapshot (absent → v1_manifest false), and recall-vs-defects.sh's fixture-head fallback resolves to manifests/<pr>/head.
findings.failure_mode: Grades against the v1 label set carry corpus_sha256 null and a wrong fixture root, so the three label sets FR-2 compares are not graded under the same provenance rules.
findings.suggested_fix: Return the parent manifests/ directory for both 'c131' and 'v1' in key_set_root (`label_set(t) in ("c131", "v1")`) and mirror that in recall-vs-defects.sh's set_root test, or state explicitly that v1 is never a grading key.

findings.cross_file_justification: ablation-grade.sh's grade_union docstring (in diff) describes meta/cell.json sessions as {id, valid, status, cost_usd, run_dir}; ablation-row.sh (in diff) additionally reads per-session attempts and attempt_costs from the same file and its --validate enforces sessions_valid <= sessions_attempted.
findings.description: sessions_attempted counts sessions with `attempts >= 1` and all_spend_usd sums attempt_costs, both read from cell.json fields the grader's contract for cell.json does not list. If run-ablation.sh writes cell.json as the grader documents it, every cell row has sessions_attempted 0 with sessions_valid >= 1 and all_spend_usd 0.
findings.failure_mode: --validate rejects every matched-cell row with 'matched cell fields inconsistent', and all_spend_usd under-reports to 0 for cells.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin cell.json's session schema in one place (the grader docstring or a schema file) including attempts and attempt_costs, and have ablation-row.sh fall back to attempts=1 and attempt_costs=[cost_usd] when a session ran (status present) but the fields are absent.

findings.description: The row's sessions_valid (`n_valid = len(valid_labels)`) counts a session only when cell.json marks it valid AND its meta/pipeline.json parses and contains a BARE phase; the grader's union counts cell.json's valid flags alone. A valid session whose pipeline.json is missing or unreadable is graded into the union but dropped from the row, which can then report status infrastructure_error (n_valid 0) while carrying a graded union recall.
findings.failure_mode: Row status/degraded and the attached union grade disagree about how many sessions were valid; the degraded reason 'sessions_valid < k/2' can fire for cells the grader considered complete.
findings.suggested_fix: Take sessions_valid from cell.json's valid flags (matching grade_union) and record a separate degraded reason when a valid session has no BARE pipeline record.
